                    ### Question
                    A previously healthy 50-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after she was observed having a seizure. On arrival, she is conscious and reports that she feels drowsy. An MRI of the brain shows a 4-cm, round, sharply demarcated mass. She undergoes resection of the mass. A photomicrograph of a section of the resected specimen is shown. This patient's mass is most likely derived from which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Neurons
opb. Astrocytes
opc. Schwann cells
opd. Arachnoid cells
ope. Oligodendrocytes

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The mass in the patient's brain is most likely derived from astrocytes. The round, sharply demarcated mass on MRI, along with the histopathological examination of the resected specimen, suggests a brain tumor. The patient's symptoms, including the seizure episode and drowsiness, are likely related to the mass effect on brain structures. The evidence path linking seizures to brain mass supports the presence of a tumor causing the seizure. Therefore, the mass is most likely derived from astrocytes.
